newsitem.title: FINLAND: Tamro 1996 sales up 23 pct to FIM 13.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Tamro 1996 sales up 23 pct to FIM 13.2 bln.

text.p: Finnish pharmaceuticals wholesaler Oy Tamro Ab said in a statement on Thursday group sales increased 23 percent in 1996 to 13.2 billion markka.
Tamro said an exceptional increase of around 800 million markka in November-December 1996 sales in Sweden had boosted end-year sales.

The exceptional rise in Swedish sales, which Tamro described as hoarding of drugs due to a change in the Swedish drug reimbursement, would "essentially decrease" sales in the early months of 1997, the company said.
On December 17, publishing January-November sales figures, Tamro forecast that 1996 sales might rise to 13 billion markka.
On Thursday, Tamro said the firming of the Swedish crown had accounted for about eight percentage points of the sales growth.
The Pharma Distribution Division's sales rose 24 percent year-on-year in 1996 to 12.3 billion markka, Tamro said.

Tamro's market share of pharmaceuticals sales in Finland rose to 63 percent in 1996 from 61 percent in 1995, but in Sweden its market share in January-November year-on-year fell to 61 percent from 62 percent, it said.
The Hospital and Laboratory Division's sales rose 23 percent year-on-year to 536 million markka. About 14 percentage points of the increase were due to acquisitions, Tamro said.
The hygiene products division Kolmi's sales rose four percent year-on-year in 1996 to 264 million markka, Tamro said. -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-6805 0245
